reviews.summary: This is the one greeting-card line in the list. It could go to anyone, which breaks VOICE.md's rule on sincere, specific sample lines, and it's the line in the list that looks like padding to reach 20.; The very next block is the free Letter template, so a reader would assume the free letter can be scheduled. Scheduling is premium only (messages/en.json scheduleHelp: "Premium.").

Scheduling is premium only (publish.ts: options.schedule forces needsUnlock; en.json scheduleHelp ends 'Premium.'). Placed just above The Letter's 'free, tonight, without paying', the current line implies the free letter can be timed.; The same scheduling fix, in Spanish.; 'He's noticed' reads first as 'he has noticed', which flips the meaning.; This matches the English fix. Without 'en él', the reader can't tell what you've noticed.; The English wordplay doesn't survive. In Spanish, 'lo intenta' refers back to 'impresionarme', so the line says he isn't trying to impress you and then that he is. 'Recuerdo pensar' is also a calque.; This is a different question from the English ('How can I tell my boyfriend how I feel in a letter?'), and the answer doesn't fit it: he's already her boyfriend

That's the emotional intent behind the search, and the post never names it.; Answers the "make him cry" intent directly with the post's own method, so it gives more than the lists that only promise tears.; Spanish PAA asks twice for a letter "que lo haga llorar". reviews.summary: In Spain 'te dejaste X' means 'you forgot X'. Item 13 uses that sense ('Sabía que te lo ibas a dejar'), so here it reads as 'you forgot the last of the milk' and the kindness is lost. 'La última leche' is also not idiomatic.; The English says 'He taps'. The Spanish imperative 'Toca' is addressed to the reader, so it reads as an instruction to her rather than a description of what he sees.; 'Eras tú' reads as 'the stranger was you'. The English 'That was you' means he was the reason, and 'Fue culpa tuya' says that in natural Spain Spanish.

Mirrors the Spanish fix so EN and ES stay in step, and speaks to the 'express my feelings to a guy I love' reader who isn't settled with him yet.; The Spanish PAA '¿Cómo enamorar a un hombre con una carta?' is the only one of the 11 questions (EN and ES) still not answered in the body, the FAQ or by a link. The new-boyfriend letter is already the answer; the page just needs to say so in the words people search with.
